# Artefaktkatalog

[English](ARTIFACTS.md) | Deutsch

<!-- Generated file. Do not edit. -->

Erzeugt aus catalog/ durch scripts/gen_artifact_docs.py. Nicht von Hand bearbeiten: die CI erzeugt diese Datei neu und schlägt fehl, wenn sie abweicht.

623 Artefakte über 31 Agent(en), davon 498 auf einer abgerufenen Herstellerquelle beruhend.

Als unbestätigt markierte Einträge werden trotzdem gesammelt, aber keine Herstellerquelle bestätigt den Pfad. Das Fehlen eines solchen Artefakts ist daher kein Beweis dafür, dass der Agent nicht genutzt wurde, sondern unklar.

Ein mit [unbelegt] markierter Pfad gehört zu einem bestätigten Eintrag, dessen Quelle genau diesen Pfad nicht nennt. Er wird wie jeder andere Pfad gesammelt, und ein Fehlschlag unter ihm ist genauso unklar wie bei einem unbestätigten Eintrag.

Was bestätigt hier bedeutet: der Eintrag wurde anhand der in seiner Zeile verlinkten Quelle geschrieben, und das Schema erlaubt für diese Markierung nur die Dokumentation oder den Quellcode des Herstellers. Es bedeutet nicht, dass eine zweite Person die Seite geöffnet und bestätigt hat, dass dort genau dieser Pfad steht; diesen Durchgang hat der Katalog noch nicht hinter sich. Eine bestätigte Zeile ist also belegt, aber nicht unabhängig geprüft. Folgen Sie dem Link, wenn eine Schlussfolgerung am Pfad hängt.

## Amazon Q Developer (CLI and IDE extension)

Vendor: Amazon

[EN] Amazon's coding agent, in a command line form and an IDE extension form. The command line form has been renamed and continues under the vendor's newer product name, but the vendor states that product still reads these directories, so these paths remain live evidence. This is the better documented of the two because the command line source is public and the paths can be read out of the code that builds them. The richest artifact is not a transcript: each conversation gets its own bare git repository under the home directory holding tagged snapshots of the user's working tree, so the content of files the agent created, changed or deleted is recoverable long after the working copy is gone, and it joins to the conversation record by identifier. Two traps that make an analyst conclude nothing happened. The authentication keys are spelled odic rather than oidc, so the obvious search finds nothing and the user looks unauthenticated. And the logs are deleted rather than rotated when they reach their size limit, with no predecessor file left behind.

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `Q_CLI_DATA_DIR`: [EN] Overrides the local data directory that holds data.sqlite3 and settings.json. If set, every conversation, the shell command history table and the stored auth tokens move somewhere the catalogue cannot predict, and a collection of the documented locations returns an empty result that looks exactly like 'the CLI was never used'. Read it from the live environment and from shell profiles. Trap: only the newer agent crate honours it. The chat-cli crate computes the same paths from dirs::data_local_dir() directly and ignores the variable, so depending on the installed version the override may apply to one component and not the other.
- `XDG_DATA_HOME`: [EN] On Linux the data directory is computed from dirs::data_local_dir(), which honours XDG_DATA_HOME. If it is set, data.sqlite3 and settings.json are under $XDG_DATA_HOME/amazon-q rather than ~/.local/share/amazon-q. This is a stock XDG variable that is often set by distributions and dotfile frameworks, so it is a realistic miss rather than a theoretical one.
- `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`: [EN] On Unix the log directory is runtime_dir()/qlog, where runtime_dir() prefers dirs::runtime_dir() (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR). Normally a tmpfs under /run/user/<uid>, so the logs do not survive logout and cannot be recovered from a disk image.
- `TMPDIR`: [EN] Falls back to TMPDIR when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset, and on macOS then to the Darwin per-user temp directory from confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR), which is a /var/folders/... path that differs per user and per boot. The log directory therefore cannot be reconstructed offline with confidence and must be resolved live.
- `Q_LOG_LEVEL`: [EN] Sets log verbosity. The vendor documentation states logs are always written to files regardless of verbosity flags, but the level still governs how much detail lands there, and the vendor's own MCP troubleshooting text tells users to re-run with Q_LOG_LEVEL=trace, which produces logs with far more prompt and tool detail.
- `Q_LOG_STDOUT`: [EN] Redirects logging to stdout. Combined with a shell redirection this can put a full log wherever the operator chose, outside any catalogued path.
- `Q_DISABLE_TELEMETRY`: [EN] Disables telemetry collection. Does not move any artifact, but it explains an absence: no telemetry-cognito-credentials entry in the state table and no telemetry traffic is consistent with this being set rather than with the tool being unused.
- `Q_ZDOTDIR`: [EN] Overrides ZDOTDIR for the CLI's shell integration. Changes which zsh dotfile directory the integration reads and writes, so shell-integration evidence and any injected hooks may sit outside the user's normal ~/.zshrc and friends.
- `HOME`: [EN] Everything under ~/.aws/amazonq (prompt history, prompts, agents, legacy MCP config, checkpoints, knowledge bases, IDE chat history) and ~/.aws/sso/cache is resolved from the home directory. A service account, a container, a sudo invocation or an SSH session with a different HOME puts a complete second copy of the agent's history in a place nobody is looking. Enumerate all home directories on the endpoint, not just the interactive user's.
- `USERPROFILE`: [EN] Everything under ~/.aws/amazonq (prompt history, prompts, agents, legacy MCP config, checkpoints, knowledge bases, IDE chat history) and ~/.aws/sso/cache is resolved from the home directory. A service account, a container, a sudo invocation or an SSH session with a different HOME puts a complete second copy of the agent's history in a place nobody is looking. Enumerate all home directories on the endpoint, not just the interactive user's.

## Amp

Vendor: Sourcegraph

<https://github.com/Eric-Song-Nop/agentstat/blob/main/AGENTS_MONITORING_SOLUTIONS.md>, <https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/auth.go>, <https://github.com/plurigrid/asi/blob/main/skills/amp-continue/SKILL.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/janekbaraniewski/openusage/main/docs/site/docs/providers/amp.md>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `AMP_DISABLE_AMP_THREAD_TRAILER`: [EN] Removes the thread identifier this agent otherwise writes into every commit it makes. That trailer is the link between a commit in a repository and the conversation that produced it, and it is frequently the only place that link exists, because the conversation itself is not necessarily on the endpoint. Set, the commits look like anybody's. An investigation that concludes from clean trailers that no agent touched a repository has to rule this variable out first, and the same switch exists as a setting in the configuration file this catalogue collects.
- `AMP_DISABLE_AMP_COAUTHOR_TRAILER`: [EN] The same shape for the co-author trailer, which is the other half of the attribution this product writes into git history. Both default to on, so both being absent from a repository that the agent worked in is a question rather than an answer.
- `AMP_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK`: [EN] Turns off update checking, overriding the setting that does the same. It matters here only because the update path is one of the few things that write to the install tree, so a version that stopped moving while the agent kept running is explained by this rather than by the product being unused.

### first

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

## Claude Code

Vendor: Anthropic

[EN] Anthropic's terminal coding agent, also reachable from the desktop app, VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, the Agent SDK and CI. It keeps by far the richest on-disk record of any agent covered here: full transcripts, every prompt typed, pre-edit file snapshots, subagent activity, permission decisions and effective policy.

<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory>, <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings>, <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions>, <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the shared credential and profile directory that Claude Code and the agent SDK both read. The vendor's reference gives the resolution order as this variable first, then ~/.config/anthropic on Linux and macOS, then the Anthropic directory under %APPDATA% on Windows. A collection that reads only the default two reports no federated identity on a host that has one.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DEBUG_LOGS_DIR`: [EN] Moves the debug log. Despite the name it is a file path and not a directory, and the vendor states the default as ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt. Debug logging also has to be enabled separately, so an absent log is the normal state rather than a sign of anything.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`: [EN] Moves the plugins root. Despite the name it sets the parent directory, with the marketplace registry and the plugin cache in subdirectories under it, and the vendor states the default as ~/.claude/plugins. Plugins are executable code the agent loads, so a relocated root is a hole in exactly the evidence that answers what the agent was made to do.
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: [EN] Moves the whole configuration directory away from ~/.claude, taking settings, transcripts, prompt history and plugins with it. A collection keyed on ~/.claude alone finds nothing on such a host, which is indistinguishable from the agent never having run. Read the variable from the shell profile and from process environment evidence before concluding an agent was absent.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY`: [EN] Suppresses writing to history.jsonl. Its presence in a shell profile is itself a finding, since prompt history normally outlives the transcripts.

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

One small file per RUNNING session; Claude Code removes each file when its session exits and clears crash leftovers on the next launch.  NOT part of the age-based sweep. One small file per RUNNING session; each file is removed when its session exits, and crash leftovers are cleared on the next launch. Live-response only - a file here means either a session running right now or one that died uncleanly (changelog v2.1.246 fixed headless sessions failing to clean up stale entries). | bestätigt | [official](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md) |

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

### durable

**Meist noch vorhanden.** Vom Aufräumlauf nicht erfasst und überleben damit regelmässig die Transkripte, die sie beschreiben. Sind die Transkripte schon weg, ist diese Gruppe das, was bleibt, und sie genügt oft, um zu belegen, dass ein Agent lief, was er durfte und was gefragt wurde.

### Veraltete Pfade

Die folgenden Pfade werden von aktuellen Versionen nicht mehr geschrieben oder gelesen. Sie werden trotzdem gesammelt, weil sie eine ältere Installation belegen, dürfen aber nie als aktueller Zustand dargestellt werden.

- `claude_code.legacy_state_dirs`: `~/.claude/todos/`, `~/.claude/statsig/`, `~/.claude/logs/`

## Claude Desktop

Vendor: Anthropic

[EN] Anthropic's desktop application, which is now one application with a chat surface, an agentic surface called Cowork and a surface that runs the Claude Code command line agent, so on an endpoint it is no longer cleanly separable from that command line product: several paths belong to both and the catalogue says which. Four things decide what a collection means here. The vendor's own page documenting the on-disk layout is written for a managed third-party deployment whose directory carries a distinct name, and a sibling page states that a standard install uses the same layout under the ordinary name, which is why the standard spellings in this file are marked unsourced rather than dropped. On Windows the root is genuinely uncertain: the vendor states one location, documents a completed move to another for the managed build, and a packaged install redirects writes to a third under a package container, so probe all three and record which had content. Every entry here now searches the package container wherever it searches the roaming path, because the redirection is the package virtualization itself rather than a judgement about this product; those spellings are marked unsourced, and a test fails if one of them goes missing. Until that was done, three entries of twenty searched the container and the rest did not, so a store install returned nothing for the audit log, the session files and the memory while the paths looked complete. Every Cowork and chat session carries an append-only event log whose entries are chained so that deletions are detectable, which is the closest thing to a tamper-evident record any agent in this catalogue offers, and verifying it needs a key that only a live host can decrypt. And an organization can set a retention period that deletes whole idle sessions with their attached files, so an absent conversation may be policy rather than anything a user did.

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: [EN] Moves the whole Claude Code configuration directory away from ~/.claude. Claude Desktop's Code tab runs an embedded Claude Code, so this relocates the Code tab conversation transcripts (projects/), the desktop app's scheduled-task SKILL.md files, plugins and the .credentials.json store. A collection that only walks ~/.claude will find nothing on a machine where this is set, while the desktop app's own store under the Claude application-data directory is unaffected.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME`: [EN] Only honoured together with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Replaces the working-directory-derived name of the projects/ subdirectory, so the usual path-encoding rule (slashes to dashes) no longer maps a transcript folder back to the project it came from.
- `CLAUDE_DESKTOP_ADD_REPO`: [EN] Read from /etc/default/claude-desktop on Linux. Set to false, the .deb does not register Anthropic's apt repository, so /etc/apt/sources.list.d/claude-desktop.list and the keyring file are absent and the usual Linux install evidence is missing even though the app is installed.
- `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`: [EN] Substituted into a plugin's .mcp.json command path and resolves to that plugin's directory. Tells an analyst which on-disk plugin directory an MCP server entry was launched from.

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

### durable

**Meist noch vorhanden.** Vom Aufräumlauf nicht erfasst und überleben damit regelmässig die Transkripte, die sie beschreiben. Sind die Transkripte schon weg, ist diese Gruppe das, was bleibt, und sie genügt oft, um zu belegen, dass ein Agent lief, was er durfte und was gefragt wurde.

## Cline

Vendor: Cline

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/apps/vscode/package.json>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/apps/vscode/src/core/storage/disk.ts>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/apps/vscode/src/shared/storage/storage-context.ts>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/docs/enterprise-solutions/monitoring/prompt-storage.mdx>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `CLINE_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the agent's entire home directory, which the resolver otherwise builds as .cline under the home directory. Everything else on this list hangs off it, so a collection keyed on ~/.cline finds nothing on such a host and cannot tell that apart from the agent never having run. The directory can also be set programmatically by the embedding application, in which case no environment variable records it.
- `CLINE_DATA_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the data directory, which holds the session transcripts, the task store, the databases, the secrets file and the settings. Set independently of the home directory, so a host can have the configuration tree in the default place and the evidence somewhere else entirely.
- `CLINE_SESSION_DATA_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the session store on its own. This is the conversation record, so it is the single most consequential variable on this list for an investigation.
- `CLINE_TEAM_DATA_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the shared team configuration tree.
- `CLINE_CONNECTOR_DATA_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the connector tree, which holds the connector settings and the per-channel logs of what the agent sent outward.
- `CLINE_CONNECTOR_SETTINGS_PATH`: [EN] Moves the connector settings file on its own, independently of the connector tree.
- `CLINE_DB_DATA_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the database directory that holds the task, cron and connector databases.
- `CLINE_TASKS_DB_PATH`: [EN] Moves the task database, one of the two transcript stores, on its own.
- `CLINE_CRON_DB_PATH`: [EN] Moves the cron database on its own. That database is the record of scheduled autonomous runs, so losing it loses the explanation for a session nobody started by hand.
- `CLINE_CONNECTORS_DB_PATH`: [EN] Moves the connector database on its own.
- `CLINE_HOOKS_LOG_PATH`: [EN] Moves the hook audit log, the one artifact that dates a prompt, to any path at all rather than to a directory under the data root. A collection that searches only the data directory finds nothing on such a host, and the absence looks exactly like an agent that ran without hooks. Read by the audit writer, by the session manifest store and by the team child session manager, all three of which fall back to the data directory's logs folder when it is unset.
- `CLINE_GLOBAL_SETTINGS_PATH`: [EN] Moves the global settings file, which is where an approval or a permission relaxation would be recorded.
- `CLINE_MCP_SETTINGS_PATH`: [EN] Moves the MCP server inventory, which is the list of external tools the agent could reach and often carries their credentials inline.
- `CLINE_PROVIDER_SETTINGS_PATH`: [EN] Moves the provider settings file, which records which model endpoint the agent was talking to.

### first

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

| `cline.agent_schedules` | agent schedules | config | macOS, Linux, Windows | `~/.cline/schedules/` | json | normal | [EN] A schedule the agent created for itself, so it persists until something removes it. Removing the schedule removes the only record of why a run happened, while the run's own transcript stays in the session store, which is the pairing to look for. | bestätigt | [source_code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts) |
| `cline.chat_workspace` | chat workspace | file_snapshot | macOS, Linux, Windows | `~/.cline/data/workspaces/chat/` | directory | normal | [EN] The resolver's comment says this lives under the data directory rather than the operating system temporary directory precisely so that temp reapers never delete it, which means work here survives a reboot and is not cleaned up on its own. | bestätigt | [source_code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts) |

### durable

**Meist noch vorhanden.** Vom Aufräumlauf nicht erfasst und überleben damit regelmässig die Transkripte, die sie beschreiben. Sind die Transkripte schon weg, ist diese Gruppe das, was bleibt, und sie genügt oft, um zu belegen, dass ein Agent lief, was er durfte und was gefragt wurde.

| Kennung | Name | Kategorie | Betriebssysteme | Pfade | Format | Sensitivität | Aufbewahrung | Status | Quelle |

It is opened with appendFileSync on every event, so it grows across sessions and holds runs whose session directory may be long gone. | bestätigt | [source_code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/sdk/packages/core/src/hooks/hook-file-hooks.ts) |

Die folgenden Pfade werden von aktuellen Versionen nicht mehr geschrieben oder gelesen. Sie werden trotzdem gesammelt, weil sie eine ältere Installation belegen, dürfen aber nie als aktueller Zustand dargestellt werden.

## OpenAI Codex CLI

Vendor: OpenAI

[EN] The Codex command line agent, and the Codex app and IDE extension that share its data
tree. One directory holds the conversations, the prompt history, seven SQLite state
databases and the credentials, which makes it the richest single tree of any agent here
after Claude Code.

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/core/config.schema.json>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/rollout/src/lib.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/rollout/src/recorder.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/rollout/src/list.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/rollout/src/compression.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/state/src/lib.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/state/src/sqlite.rs>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `CODEX_HOME`: [EN] Moves the whole Codex directory away from ~/.codex, taking the rollouts, the prompt history, the state databases and auth.json with it. A collection keyed on ~/.codex alone finds nothing on such a host, which is indistinguishable from Codex never having run. Resolved by find_codex_home(), which falls back to ~/.codex.
- `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME`: [EN] Moves only the SQLite state databases out of the Codex home, so the rollouts can be present while the thread index, the logs database and the memories are somewhere else entirely. The constant is SQLITE_HOME_ENV = "CODEX_SQLITE_HOME".

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

| `codex.sqlite_write_ahead_logs` | sqlite write ahead logs | transcript | macOS, Windows, Linux | `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\*.sqlite-shm` [unbelegt]<br>`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\*.sqlite-wal` [unbelegt]<br>`~/.codex/*.sqlite-shm` [unbelegt]<br>`~/.codex/*.sqlite-wal` [unbelegt] | binary | normal | [EN] Destroyed by a clean shutdown. Every Codex database is opened with journal_mode(SqliteJournalMode::Wal), so the newest writes live in the -wal sidecar until a checkpoint folds them into the main file. Collect the sidecars together with the database or lose the most recent activity, which is usually the activity under investigation. | bestätigt | [source_code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/state/src/sqlite.rs) |

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

The schema documents history.max_bytes as "If set, the maximum size of the history file in bytes. The oldest entries are dropped once the file exceeds this limit", so on a busy host the earliest prompts are already gone and the file gives no sign of how many. | bestätigt | [source_code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/core/config.schema.json) |

## GitHub Copilot CLI

Vendor: GitHub

[EN] The Copilot command line agent. GitHub documents the whole configuration directory file
by file, including which files hold credentials and what is lost by deleting each one,
which makes this one of the few agents where the catalogue rests on the vendor's own
inventory rather than on reading its source.

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/copilot-cli/main/README.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/master/plugins/mcp-server/src/com/intellij/mcpserver/impl/McpClientDetector.kt>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `COPILOT_HOME`: [EN] Overrides the default ~/.copilot location, and the CLI then reads all configuration from there. A collection keyed on ~/.copilot alone finds nothing on such a host, which is indistinguishable from Copilot CLI never having run.
- `COPILOT_CACHE_HOME`: [EN] Moves the cache directory, which otherwise follows platform convention rather than sitting under ~/.copilot. Only ephemeral data, but it is where marketplace and auto-update material lands.
- `COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG`: [EN] Moves providers.json, the registry of bring-your-own-key providers and models. Relevant to a data-egress question: it names the endpoints the agent was configured to talk to, and this variable can put that file anywhere.

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

| Kennung | Name | Kategorie | Betriebssysteme | Pfade | Format | Sensitivität | Aufbewahrung | Status | Quelle |

Documented as "Lock files and state for IDE integrations" that are "automatically managed", which is another way of saying they will not be there later. | bestätigt | [official](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference.md) |
| `copilot.session_store_sidecars` | session store sidecars | transcript | macOS, Windows, Linux | `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\session-store.db-shm`<br>`%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\session-store.db-wal`<br>`~/.copilot/session-store.db-shm`<br>`~/.copilot/session-store.db-wal` | binary | normal | [EN] If present, destroyed by a clean shutdown, and holding writes that are not yet in the database file. | **unbestätigt** | [official](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference.md) |

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

One user action, no second copy. | bestätigt | [official](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference.md) |

## Cross-cutting evidence

[EN] Evidence that belongs to no single agent: shell history showing how an agent was invoked and with which flags, package manager traces proving it was installed, and the instruction-file conventions that several agents read, which are the surface through which injected instructions reach an agent.

<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup>, <https://github.com/Adyen/adyen-web/blob/main/.windsurf/rules/code-guide.md>, <https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/.clinerules/hooks/README.md>, <https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/docs/customization/cline-rules.mdx>

### first

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

| Kennung | Name | Kategorie | Betriebssysteme | Pfade | Format | Sensitivität | Aufbewahrung | Status | Quelle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `crosscutting.npm_debug_logs` | npm debug logs | log | macOS, Linux, Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache\_logs\*-debug-*.log` [unbelegt]<br>`~/.npm/_logs/*-debug-*.log` [unbelegt] | text | normal | [EN] PRUNED AGGRESSIVELY - COLLECT FIRST. Verbatim: "Log files will be removed from the logs-dir when the number of log files exceeds logs-max, with the oldest logs being deleted first." logs-max defaults to 10 (visible as `logs-max:10` in npm's own log-file test snapshot), so roughly the last ten npm invocations survive. On a busy dev box that can be hours. | bestätigt | [official](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/npm/cli/latest/docs/lib/content/using-npm/logging.md) |
| `crosscutting.npm_global_install_dirs` | npm global install dirs | install_evidence | macOS, Linux, Windows | `%APPDATA%\npm\`<br>`%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\`<br>`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/` [unbelegt]<br>`/usr/local/bin/`<br>`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/`<br>`~/.nvm/versions/node/*/lib/node_modules/` [unbelegt] | json | normal | [EN] Overwritten in place on upgrade, so the installed version reflects only the CURRENT state; use ~/.npm/_logs for the install history. | bestätigt | [official](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/npm/cli/latest/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/folders.md) |

## Cursor

Vendor: Anysphere

[EN] A closed-source editor derived from VS Code, whose agent keeps its data in two trees: the editor's own user data directory, which follows the layout it inherited, and a per-user agent directory under the home directory. The vendor documents the second tree's configuration files thoroughly and documents nothing at all about where conversations are stored, which is why the transcript entries here rest on independent research and are marked unverified. Two negative findings from the vendor's own pages are worth knowing before an acquisition. There is no first-party statement that privacy mode changes what is written to local disk: it is documented as a control over cloud training and retention, so a privacy-mode user's conversations should still be expected on the endpoint. And there is no documented way to export or delete local conversation history, with account deletion explicitly leaving local data in place, so material can outlive the account it belongs to.

<https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview>, <https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions>, <https://github.com/AltimateAI/vscode-dbt-power-user/blob/5fc912ee821cf1e42feb826ad48f9a01e2e98a80/documentation/docs/setup/cursor_installation_workaround.md>, <https://github.com/pradipta/wallfacer/blob/94a58b79a47c4e815e60ffe6bfc5fb604351d2c3/internal/agent/cursor/cursor.go>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/a2de475d2ee3a2f00865944c79c15600c1ada45c/docs/teardowns/2026-07-11-cursor-product-teardown.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VasiHemanth/tokentelemetry/0d691ae343ed31991e504a738bb1b288eea3b2ee/docs/research/harness-survey/harness-cursor-vscode.md>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the command line agent's whole directory. Its own code reads this variable and falls back to the product directory under the home only when it is unset, and every subdirectory is built from the result, the per-project directory among them. So a host with this set keeps its agent state somewhere this catalogue cannot predict, and a collection of the default path returns nothing while reporting success. The self-hosted worker takes the same variable and documents its own default besides.
- `CURSOR_SANDBOX_POLICY_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the directory of sandbox policies, which is where the rules that decide what the agent may run without asking are kept. Its own code resolves this variable first and falls back to the directory under the product's home. A policy set here and collected from the default path reads as no policy in force.
- `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the agent configuration directory that the command line interface reads, which the vendor otherwise resolves to .cursor under the home directory or, on Linux and BSD, to a cursor directory under the base configuration directory. A collection keyed on the default finds nothing on such a host.
- `CURSOR_TRANSCRIPT_PATH`: [EN] Not a relocation the user sets but a value the agent passes to a hook script, holding the path of the conversation transcript for that run. It is the only documented way to learn where a transcript actually is, because the vendor states no path for one. The vendor also says it is present only when transcripts are enabled, so its absence means the feature was off rather than that the run had no conversation.

### durable

**Meist noch vorhanden.** Vom Aufräumlauf nicht erfasst und überleben damit regelmässig die Transkripte, die sie beschreiben. Sind die Transkripte schon weg, ist diese Gruppe das, was bleibt, und sie genügt oft, um zu belegen, dass ein Agent lief, was er durfte und was gefragt wurde.

## Gemini CLI

Vendor: Google

[EN] Google's command line agent. The one agent in this catalogue that documents an automatic
deletion policy for its own conversations, which changes what a collection means: the
default is to delete chats older than thirty days, so an absent conversation is the
expected state rather than a sign that anybody removed it.

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/main/docs/reference/configuration.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/main/packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`: [EN] Relocates the whole .gemini directory. homedir() in packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts returns this value when it is set and the user's home directory otherwise, so a collection keyed on ~/.gemini finds nothing on such a host and cannot tell that apart from Gemini CLI never having run.
- `GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH`: [EN] Moves the machine-wide settings file, which is where an administrator would enforce policy. Reading only the documented location can therefore report no policy on a host that has one.
- `GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS_PATH`: [EN] Moves the machine-wide defaults file, the lowest layer of the four-layer settings stack.
- `GEMINI_CLI_TRUSTED_FOLDERS_PATH`: [EN] Moves trustedFolders.json, the record of which directories the user allowed the agent to work in. That record is the answer to what the agent was permitted to touch.
- `SANDBOX`: [EN] Not a relocation variable the vendor offers, but the one that decides where the runtime state is. Storage.getGlobalRuntimeDir() in packages/core/src/config/storage.ts returns ~/.cache/.gemini when SANDBOX is 'sandbox-exec', which is macOS Seatbelt, and ~/.gemini otherwise, because the seatbelt profile blocks writes to the home directory. So on a sandboxed macOS host the chats, the prompt log, the project registry and the per-project temporary trees are all under ~/.cache/.gemini and a collection of ~/.gemini alone finds the configuration and none of the history. Any other value means a container, where the launcher mounts an ephemeral directory at the ordinary location.
- `GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD`: [EN] Replaces the built-in system prompt with a file of the operator's choosing, anywhere on disk. Prompt-injection surface that lives outside every directory this catalogue names: follow the value.

## Goose

Vendor: Block

[EN] The Goose command line agent and the Goose desktop app, which share one configuration
tree and one session store. Three things make this family awkward and all three cost
evidence if they are not known. The product keeps its data in three directories rather
than one, splitting configuration, data and state the way the freedesktop specification
does, so the conversations and the logs are not siblings. macOS has two trees rather than
one: the vendor's environment guide gives the application support directory as the macOS
root, while the code at the library version the lockfile pins resolves macOS to the same
freedesktop directories as Linux, so an upgraded machine can hold both and a recent
install holds only the second. And one environment variable relocates all of it at once.

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/block/goose/main/documentation/docs/guides/config-files.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/block/goose/main/documentation/docs/guides/environment-variables.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/block/goose/main/documentation/docs/guides/logs.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/block/goose/main/documentation/docs/guides/recipes/session-recipes.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/block/goose/main/documentation/docs/guides/context-engineering/index.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/block/goose/main/crates/goose/src/config/paths.rs>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT`: [EN] Moves the whole tree. config/paths.rs reads this variable first and, when it holds an absolute path, builds every directory under it as <root>/config, <root>/data, <root>/state and <root>/.agents, ignoring the platform defaults entirely. A relative value is discarded and the defaults apply, which the module has a test for. Every path in this file is then wrong by exactly one prefix, and a collection keyed on the defaults reports an agent that never ran.
- `GOOSE_MOIM_MESSAGE_FILE`: [EN] Names a file whose contents are injected into the model's working memory on every turn, anywhere on disk. It is standing instructions to the agent at a path nothing else in this catalogue records, so it is collected only if somebody reads the variable off the environment first. The vendor's own example of what belongs in it is a set of security guardrails, which makes its absence or its alteration the difference between an agent that was told not to send code off the machine and one that was not.
- `GOOSE_MOIM_MESSAGE_TEXT`: [EN] The same injection carried as literal text rather than as a file, concatenated with the file when both are set. There is then no file to collect at all: what the agent was told every turn exists only in the environment of the process, so look for it in shell profiles, service definitions and pipeline configuration rather than on the filesystem.
- `CONTEXT_FILE_NAMES`: [EN] Replaces the filenames that count as hint files. The default is the two this catalogue records and the variable takes a JSON array of any names at all, including another product's rule file. A collection that searches for the documented two then finds nothing while the agent was reading standing instructions out of a third filename on every turn.
- `GOOSE_RECIPE_PATH`: [EN] Additional directories recipes are read from, separated by colons on Unix and by semicolons on Windows. No default recipe directory is documented at all, so this variable is frequently the only record of where the reusable agent runs on a host actually live.
- `GOOSE_RECIPE_GITHUB_REPO`: [EN] A repository recipes are searched in, given as an owner and a name. A recipe that ran from there was never on the endpoint as a file, so the instruction the agent followed is in no filesystem collection and the session record is the only local trace of it.
- `GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING`: [EN] Decides whether the provider credentials exist on disk at all. Unset, the secrets are in the operating system's keyring and there is no file; set to anything, the product writes them to secrets.yaml in plain text. So this variable is what turns the credential entry in this file from something that is never there into something that is, and its presence in a profile is itself worth reporting.

### first

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

## Hermes

Vendor: Hermes

[EN] A self-hosted agent that runs as a long-lived process rather than as a command a person types, which is why its evidence is shaped the way it is: one home directory holds everything, and the same home is reachable from a chat platform as well as from the terminal.

Where that home is decides whether a collection finds anything at all, and it is not the same on every platform. The agent resolves it as an in-process override, then the HERMES_HOME variable, then a platform default, and the platform default is ~/.hermes on macOS and Linux but %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes on Windows. The user guide says ~/.hermes throughout and never mentions the Windows location, so a catalogue built from the documentation alone points every Windows path at a directory the product never creates and reports a clean endpoint. Both spellings are listed on every entry for that reason. Installed inside WSL2 the agent is a Linux install and lives at ~/.hermes inside the distribution's filesystem, which a collection of the Windows volume does not reach.

The home can also exist several times over. A named profile is a complete second home at <home>/profiles/<name>/, with its own configuration, credentials, memories, skills, sessions and logs, and the agent serves every live one of them at once. A collection that takes only the default home takes one agent out of however many were running, and the others look like they were never there.

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/website/docs/developer-guide/session-storage.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md>, <https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/639823919ced15640924e905bacab3858c5afd19/hermes_constants.py>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/website/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/README.md>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `HERMES_HOME`: [EN] Relocates the agent's entire directory: configuration, credentials, memories, skills, scheduled jobs, session transcripts and logs all hang off it. Every path in this file has a spelling rooted at this variable for that reason.

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

### durable

**Meist noch vorhanden.** Vom Aufräumlauf nicht erfasst und überleben damit regelmässig die Transkripte, die sie beschreiben. Sind die Transkripte schon weg, ist diese Gruppe das, was bleibt, und sie genügt oft, um zu belegen, dass ein Agent lief, was er durfte und was gefragt wurde.

| Kennung | Name | Kategorie | Betriebssysteme | Pfade | Format | Sensitivität | Aufbewahrung | Status | Quelle |

A backup the user made by hand is not pruned at all. | bestätigt | [source_code](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/639823919ced15640924e905bacab3858c5afd19/hermes_cli/backup.py) |

## Junie

Vendor: JetBrains

[EN] JetBrains' agent, inside the IDE and on the command line. Two things decide what a collection of it means. Its instruction file does not have to be where this catalogue looks: the vendor's own guidelines repository states that a project defines its guidelines in .junie/AGENTS.md or AGENTS.md and that a custom path can be set in the IDE's project settings instead, so a glob over the project can miss the file the agent actually read, and the setting has to be read off the endpoint before an absence means anything. And the vendor's documentation host answers requests but serves no text: every path on it, including the pages the community sources cite, returns the same 203 byte stub that redirects a browser to the start page, because the site renders its content with JavaScript. So the entries here that rest on a third party's reading of those pages stay unverified, and settling them needs somebody with a browser rather than another fetch.

## Kilo Code

Vendor: Kilo Code

<https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/blob/main/docs/configuration.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/main/packages/kilo-docs/pages/code-with-ai/agents/session-history.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/main/packages/kilo-docs/pages/customize/custom-modes.md>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `KILO_DB`: [EN] Moves the session database away from the documented default, so a collection keyed on the default path finds nothing on such a host. The vendor's own guidance is to ask the product where its database is rather than to assume the path.
- `XDG_DATA_HOME`: [EN] Moves the session database, which the vendor documents as living under the XDG data directory on every platform including Windows, where the documented default is the user profile joined with .local\\share.
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`: [EN] Moves the global configuration file and the global agent definitions beside it, which the vendor documents as living under the XDG configuration directory.
- `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT`: [EN] Supplies configuration as the content of an environment variable rather than as a file, and the vendor's precedence list puts it above every file. A host configured this way has the highest-priority configuration in no file at all, so a collection can be complete and still not hold what the agent was actually run with. Look for it in the shell profiles and in whatever started the process.

### normal

**Normal sichern.** Unterliegen der üblichen Aufbewahrungsfrist des Agenten, die bei mehreren Agenten standardmässig 30 Tage beträgt.

## Kiro

Vendor: Amazon

[EN] Amazon's agentic development environment, in an editor form and a command line form. The command line form is the Amazon Q Developer CLI renamed, and the vendor states it still reads the older product's configuration directories, so an Amazon Q path is live evidence in an engagement that only mentions this product and the reverse is also true: collect both trees. The split between the two matters for what can be relied on. The older product is open source and its paths can be read out of its own code, while this one is closed source since the rename, so most of what is written here rests on documentation prose. Three consequences worth knowing before an acquisition. The session database is documented only as a database somewhere in the agent's home directory, with no filename, so both candidate trees have to be swept and files matched on their SQLite header rather than on a name. The pre-approved permissions for a project live outside the project, so they outlive a working copy that has been deleted. And the wire recording variable writes a complete second transcript to a path the operator chooses, which no directory walk will find: read the variable off the endpoint.

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `KIRO_HOME`: [EN] Redirects the whole global ~/.kiro tree. The vendor states that agents, prompts, skills, steering, settings and sessions all resolve against it. If it is set, a collection that only walks ~/.kiro finds nothing at all: no transcripts, no permissions, no MCP config. Read it from the process environment, the user shell profiles and any service unit or wrapper script before concluding the agent was unused.
- `KIRO_CHAT_LOG_FILE`: [EN] Relocates the CLI chat log file to an arbitrary path, out of the platform temp directory. A collection that only sweeps $TMPDIR/kiro-log, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/kiro-log or %TEMP%\kiro-log misses it entirely, and the analyst sees no log activity.
- `KIRO_LOG_LEVEL`: [EN] Log verbosity, default error. At the default the chat log holds almost nothing, so an empty or tiny kiro-chat.log is NOT evidence that the CLI was unused. Conversely a value of debug or trace means the log may hold prompts, file paths, code snippets and command output.
- `KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH`: [EN] Path to a JSONL file recording the TUI ACP wire traffic. When set, that file is a full second copy of the conversation at an operator-chosen location that no catalogue path will predict. Treat any value seen in shell history or a wrapper script as a transcript artifact in its own right.
- `KIRO_API_KEY`: [EN] Long-lived API key credential (values are prefixed ksk_) used for non-interactive runs. It is passed through the environment, so copies commonly land in shell history, CI definitions and wrapper scripts rather than in any Kiro-owned file. Also explains sessions with no interactive sign-in.
- `TMPDIR`: [EN] On macOS the CLI log directory is $TMPDIR/kiro-log/, which on a default macOS install resolves under a per-user /var/folders/... path. The value must be captured live: the resolved directory cannot be reconstructed from a dead disk with certainty.
- `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`: [EN] On Linux the CLI log directory is $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/kiro-log/. Typically a tmpfs under /run/user/<uid> that does not survive logout or reboot, so the logs are live-response only. The vendor also documents /tmp/kiro-log/ as a fallback.
- `KIRO_LOG_NO_COLOR`: [EN] Only disables ANSI colour in log output (v1.26.0+). It does not move anything, but its presence in an environment or profile is a weak indicator that someone was collecting or post-processing Kiro logs.

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

Path and lifetime are entirely operator-chosen. | bestätigt | [official](https://kiro.dev/docs/reference/settings.md) |

## OpenCode

Vendor: OpenCode

<https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/mcp/auth.ts>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/packages/core/src/global.ts>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/packages/core/src/session/sql.ts>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `OPENCODE_DB`: [EN] Moves or renames the conversation database. database.ts path() returns the value when it is absolute, joins it to the data directory when it is relative, and honours the literal ':memory:', which means the conversations of that run are never written to disk at all. A collection keyed on the documented filename finds nothing on such a host, and with ':memory:' there is nothing to find: the absence is the finding, and it has to be read off the environment rather than off the filesystem.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB`: [EN] Decides which of two database filenames is in use. database.ts writes opencode.db for the release channels latest, beta and prod or when this variable is set, and opencode-<channel>.db otherwise, with every character outside a small set replaced by a dash. Both spellings are in this catalogue for that reason; the variable is what says which one a host should have.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`: [EN] Replaces the configuration directory outright, so the agent definitions, the commands and the configuration file are not under the documented path. global.ts make() takes the flag before the freedesktop configuration directory.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG`: [EN] Names the configuration file itself, anywhere on disk, which is the file that carries the permission set and the MCP servers.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`: [EN] Carries the configuration in the environment rather than in a file. There is then no configuration file to collect at all, and what the agent was permitted to do exists only in the process environment of the run: look for it in shell profiles, service definitions and CI configuration.
- `OPENCODE_TEST_HOME`: [EN] Replaces the home directory the product resolves everything else from, so every path in this catalogue moves with it.
- `OPENCODE_PLUGIN_META_FILE`: [EN] Names the plugin metadata file, which says which plugin code the product loads.
- `OPENCODE_MODELS_PATH`: [EN] Names the model catalogue file, which says which providers and endpoints were available to the run.
- `OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG`: [EN] Names the interface configuration file, which this catalogue otherwise expects in the configuration directory.

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

## pi

Vendor: pi

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/session-format.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/main/packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the agent's whole directory: its credentials, its model list, its settings, its extensions, its tools, its prompts, its skills, its themes, its managed binaries, its debug log and its sessions all hang off it. Every path in this file has a spelling rooted at this variable for that reason. The variable that was declared here before it moves the sessions alone, so a tree relocated with this one was collected as nothing at all while the collection reported success.

The name itself is not fixed. The product builds it from its own application name, so a fork published under another name reads another variable, keeps its directory under another dot directory and writes a debug log under another file name. Read the installed package's own configuration before concluding a host has none of this.
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`: [EN] Relocates the session transcripts. The variable's name is defined in the agent's configuration module; the documentation page that describes the session format does not state it, which is why the path rooted at it is marked unsourced.

## Qwen Code

Vendor: Qwen Team, Alibaba Group

[EN] Qwen Code is an open-source command line coding agent (npm package @qwen-code/qwen-code) that began as a fork of Google's Gemini CLI and has since diverged very far from it, adding a daemon and browser Web Shell, an SDK, workflows, subagents, managed memory and scheduled channel runs. Everything user-level lives under ~/.qwen (relocatable with QWEN_HOME, and the runtime output subset again with QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR). The one thing an analyst must know is that the conversation transcripts are NOT where the upstream layout or even the fork's own stale code comment says: they are per-session append-only JSONL under ~/.qwen/projects/<cwd-with-non-alphanumerics-replaced-by-hyphens>/chats/, they have NO retention policy and are never deleted on a schedule, while the pre-edit file backups and subagent transcripts beside them DO expire after 30 days and the raw model API logs after 7.

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `QWEN_HOME`: [EN] Replaces ~/.qwen as the global configuration directory (absolute, relative to cwd, or leading ~). Moves settings, credentials, trusted folders, MCP approvals, memory, skills, plans, file-history, the projects/ transcript tree and almost everything else in one go. Project-level .qwen directories are unaffected. An empty string counts as unset. Collect the process environment first: with this set, the default ~/.qwen holds nothing and a default-path collection returns 'agent never used'. The one exception is ~/.qwen/source.json, which the installer writes to the real home directory regardless.
- `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR`: [EN] Overrides only the runtime output base (conversations, logs, todos) while configuration stays under QWEN_HOME. Because transcripts, the tmp/<project-hash> tree, debug logs and the projects/ tree hang off the runtime base, this can split the evidence across two filesystems. It takes precedence over the runtimeOutputDir setting.
- `QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH`: [EN] Overrides the system settings file path. System settings have the highest precedence of all settings files, so the policy actually in force may be at an arbitrary path.
- `QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS_PATH`: [EN] Overrides the system defaults file path (the lowest-precedence layer).
- `QWEN_CODE_MCP_APPROVALS_PATH`: [EN] Relocates mcpApprovals.json wholesale. Set, and ~/.qwen/mcpApprovals.json is empty or absent while MCP approval decisions exist elsewhere.
- `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_BASE_DIR`: [EN] Moves the managed auto-memory base (both the projects/<...>/memory tiers and ~/.qwen/memories) away from the runtime base directory.
- `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_LOCAL`: [EN] =1 moves project auto-memory into <project>/.qwen/memory instead of under the user profile, which puts model-written memory inside the working copy where it may be committed.
- `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_PROJECT_SCOPE`: [EN] =workspace keys project auto-memory on the resolved workspace directory instead of the nearest git root, so the memory directory name for one project differs between the two modes.
- `QWEN_CODE_FORCE_ENCRYPTED_FILE_STORAGE`: [EN] =true switches MCP OAuth tokens from plaintext ~/.qwen/mcp-oauth-tokens.json to the OS keychain where available, or to ~/.qwen/mcp-oauth-tokens-v2.json with AES-256-GCM. Absence of the plaintext file then means nothing.
- `QWEN_DEBUG_LOG_FILE`: [EN] =1 turns on the per-session debug log at ~/.qwen/debug/<session-id>.txt. Unset (the normal state) makes almost every internal debug call a no-op, so an empty debug directory is expected rather than suspicious.
- `QWEN_TELEMETRY_OUTFILE`: [EN] Writes OpenTelemetry data to the named file instead of exporting it over OTLP, creating an on-disk telemetry artifact at an operator-chosen path. Pairs with QWEN_TELEMETRY_LOG_PROMPTS and QWEN_TELEMETRY_INCLUDE_SENSITIVE_SPAN_ATTRIBUTES, which decide whether prompt text lands in it.
- `QWEN_CODE_PROFILE_STARTUP`: [EN] =1 writes JSON startup timing reports to ~/.qwen/startup-perf/. Minor, but it is an extra directory under the global dir that confirms the tool ran.
- `SEATBELT_PROFILE`: [EN] Do not move artifacts but decide whether confinement ran at all and with which profile or image, including a custom profile read from <project>/.qwen/sandbox-macos-<name>.sb. Needed to answer whether a safety control was in place, and the project rejects all four from project-scoped .env files for exactly that reason.
- `QWEN_SANDBOX`: [EN] Do not move artifacts but decide whether confinement ran at all and with which profile or image, including a custom profile read from <project>/.qwen/sandbox-macos-<name>.sb. Needed to answer whether a safety control was in place, and the project rejects all four from project-scoped .env files for exactly that reason.
- `QWEN_SANDBOX_IMAGE`: [EN] Do not move artifacts but decide whether confinement ran at all and with which profile or image, including a custom profile read from <project>/.qwen/sandbox-macos-<name>.sb. Needed to answer whether a safety control was in place, and the project rejects all four from project-scoped .env files for exactly that reason.
- `QWEN_SANDBOX_NET`: [EN] Do not move artifacts but decide whether confinement ran at all and with which profile or image, including a custom profile read from <project>/.qwen/sandbox-macos-<name>.sb. Needed to answer whether a safety control was in place, and the project rejects all four from project-scoped .env files for exactly that reason.
- `TMPDIR`: [EN] The platform temporary directory, which this product reaches for in two places. The editor companion's older port files are written there and named by the editor's process id or by the port, and getGlobalQwenDir() falls back to a .qwen directory inside it when the process has no home directory at all, which is the shape a service account or a container run has. On such a host every path in this file is wrong and the whole tree is in the temporary directory instead, where the next reboot may take it.

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

## Visual Studio Code host storage

Vendor: Microsoft

[EN] Visual Studio Code and its forks, as a storage host rather than as an agent. A dozen agentic extensions keep their conversations under workspaceStorage and globalStorage or inside state.vscdb, so these paths are worth collecting even when it is not yet known which extension was installed.

<https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-discussions/discussions/748>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vscode-docs/main/docs/configure/settings.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vscode-docs/main/docs/configure/extensions/extension-marketplace.md>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `VSCODE_PORTABLE`: [EN] Turns the whole installation portable: the extensions directory becomes <value>/extensions, the shared data directory <value>/shared-data and the file policy <value>/policy.json, from environmentService.ts. A portable installation therefore keeps its data beside the application rather than in the profile, and every profile-rooted path in this catalogue's entries for this family finds nothing on such a host.
- `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS`: [EN] Replaces the extensions directory on its own, which is where every agent extension of this family lives. extensionsPath in environmentService.ts reads it before the portable variable and before the default under the profile.

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

## Warp

Vendor: Warp

[EN] A terminal that is also an agent, and a separate command line agent that shares its rule
and skill files. Two things decide how to read a collection of it. The conversations, the
prompts and the commands the agent ran are in one SQLite database, and on macOS that
database is inside an application group container, which home directory collections
routinely skip. And almost everything that steers the agent, the rules, the skills and
the MCP servers, is in files this product shares with other vendors' directories, which
it reads more widely than any other agent in this catalogue.

## Windsurf

Vendor: Cognition

[EN] The Codeium editor, renamed Devin Desktop in mid-2026, whose agent is called Cascade. Two things about its storage decide what a collection means. First, the rename: the application reads both the legacy Windsurf and Codeium paths and the new Devin paths, writes new data to the Devin paths, and copies everything from the legacy paths to the new ones the first time it runs after the upgrade. So the same content can exist in two trees and a timestamp under a Devin path may be the migration rather than the user, which makes the legacy tree the better timeline evidence where both exist. Second, the vendor documents the directories that hold conversations and memories and says nothing at all about the files inside them, which are opaque binary blobs. The one parseable record of a conversation is the transcript file the hook interface exposes, and the product keeps only the hundred most recent of those.

<https://github.com/depalmar/ai-dfir-toolkit/blob/d3cf3577f6db374b3e196e1a05c0cd6708b9655d/artifacts/docs/RESEARCH-2026-08-14.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LayerNorm/overlay-web/6cf2cbfe09e0f25ebabf9986f1566183f477a48b/docs/develop/traversing-agent-conversations.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dayearleo/windsurf-local-user-data-decryption/0e9e057aa9962284517db9c4963c5275eff7df00/SKILL.md>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/depalmar/ai-dfir-toolkit/d3cf3577f6db374b3e196e1a05c0cd6708b9655d/artifacts/catalog/codeium-windsurf.yml>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `WINDSURF_CONFIG_DIR`: [EN] Claimed by community tooling to select the configuration directory. An exhaustive search of both of the vendor's documentation corpora and every repository in its code hosting organization found no occurrence of this name, and the only variables the vendor documents are an API key and a service key, so treat it as a lead rather than as a fact. What the vendor does document, and what actually moves the tree, is one configuration directory per release channel: the stable channel under .codeium/windsurf, the next channel under .codeium/windsurf-next and the insiders channel under .codeium/windsurf-insiders. A collector that looks only at the stable directory finds nothing on a prerelease install.

### first

**Zuerst sichern.** Rotieren oder verfallen aggressiv, nach Anzahl oder bei jedem Aufräumlauf statt nach einer bequemen Frist. Einige davon zerstört die Benutzerin schon dadurch, dass sie eine weitere Sitzung startet.

## Zed

Vendor: Zed Industries

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zed-industries/zed/main/crates/agent/src/db.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zed-industries/zed/main/crates/agent_ui/src/thread_metadata_store.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zed-industries/zed/main/crates/paths/src/paths.rs>, <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zed-industries/zed/main/docs/src/ai/mcp.md>

### Verschiebende Variablen

- `FLATPAK_XDG_CONFIG_HOME`: [EN] Replaces the configuration directory outright when the editor runs as a Flatpak, so the settings file and the user-global AGENTS.md are not under the documented path at all. config_dir() in crates/paths/src/paths.rs reads it before falling back to the freedesktop directory.
- `FLATPAK_XDG_DATA_HOME`: [EN] The same for the data directory, which holds the conversation store, the prompt library and the semantic index. This catalogue already carries one Flatpak path for an older store, which is what makes the variable worth declaring: the current tree moves the same way.
- `FLATPAK_XDG_STATE_HOME`: [EN] The same for the state directory.

### live_only

**Nur am laufenden System zu holen.** Diese Artefakte existieren nur, solange der Agent oder die Sitzung läuft, oder werden beim saubern Herunterfahren zerstört. Aus einem abgeschalteten Abbild sind sie nicht wiederherstellbar. Läuft das Endgerät noch, dann hier anfangen.

If ZED_STATELESS is set, an in-memory database is used and NOTHING is persisted.
